mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals economic weakness, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in high UNRATE periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (below 1.5%) and low unemployment rate (below 4.0%) indicates a strong economic expansion with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for the joint condition remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in the low FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE condition are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
